# Theme ideas and recorded designs

Settings offers Studio, Obsession Mode and Cartridge Quest. Studio is the rebuilt-shell registration; the latter two are allowlisted composition presentations. The rest of this catalog records design intent and experiments, not a list of downloads.

Canvas has a development cohort of 27 baseline ports with saved/stock compositions. They don't restore retired stylesheets or register all those themes in ordinary builds. See [port evidence](CANVAS_THEME_PORT_BASELINE_EVIDENCE.md), [future work](CANVAS_THEME_PORT_BACKLOG.md) and [the runtime rules](THEME_SYSTEM.md).

## Pixelody Studio

Studio gives the library, stage and inspector their own rounded windows, with a floating player and collapsible side cabinets. Blue-black surfaces, periwinkle actions and cyan confirmed state leave artwork and titles readable. Pixel type is an occasional identity accent. Keep the depth in spacing, light and a few surface levels; ordinary text doesn't need another box. Widths persist, keyboard access and cabinet recovery stay direct, and motion has static equivalents.

## Orbital Retro-Future

A spacecraft-style audio console with teal-black surfaces, yellow framing, cyan signals and small coral alerts. Instrument panels and target markers give it structure without turning the library into a flight simulator. Album art and familiar controls stay prominent; signal sweeps should be measured. Use original framing rather than franchise imagery or a wall of stars.

## Bulkhead Terminal

Charcoal bulkheads, worn gray panels, amber and terminal green make a heavier industrial console. Compact technical type, including the licensed Kenney Future face where appropriate, fits the CRT fields and hazard rails. Panels deploy and lock into place deliberately. Keep it separate from Graphite Loadout's lighter acid-tech equipment language.

## Graphite Loadout

Graphite Loadout treats the player as molded audio equipment: matte nylon, black polymer, pale stone-like controls and thin spectral edges. Most of the interface stays neutral graphite, fog gray, muted navy or industrial blue (about 85–90 percent); lime marks state, cyan carries signal data and orange is a small equipment warning.

Hard panels, clipped corners, bold track numbers and mono technical labels suit the equipment feel. Texture belongs to a material or section, not over everything. Quick snaps, card slides and brief routing feedback can support use; endless wiring, gamer RGB and shooter clutter can't. Keep the sound controls large and use original assets.

## Cartridge Quest

Playlists become cartridges, the hero resembles a title screen, and the track list borrows RPG menu navigation. Dark CRT navy and graphite housings surround recessed gray bays; pale plastic belongs to raised headers and physical controls. Violet, yellow and green distinguish actions, rewards and status. The bundled Geist Pixel type needs enough size to stay readable.

The detail choices are 8-bit, 16-bit and Arcade. Original console fixtures, pixel landscapes, cursors and short stepped responses give it character without changing the shared audio workflow. Local listening XP awards 10 points per minute of actual playback; the no-skip timer follows naturally advancing tracks. Motion-off retains static feedback. Avoid copied consoles, game sprites, franchise marks and tiny text.

## Sakura Bloom

A shaded hanami room with sage-washi surfaces, dark ink/plum lacquer, branch brown and soft green state. CSS blossoms and a little petal pink frame the music without covering the artwork. Calm drift and chime-like feedback can suit acoustic, piano, ambient or study listening; motion-off keeps a static floral treatment. Keep contrast in the controls and leave out franchise images and tourist-poster styling.

## Lo-Fi Café

Dark walnut structure, paper-soft listening surfaces and amber playback light make a quiet second-monitor nook. Moss status and muted rain-glass blue-gray prevent it becoming one brown wash. Licensed café/study photography supplies atmosphere, with restrained steam/progress motion and static substitutes. It suits writing, jazz, acoustic and lo-fi sessions. Avoid muddy contrast, novelty handwriting, sepia everywhere or a pile of café props.

## ASCII Social

A dark desktop media skin with a few large original ASCII faces and tactile panels. Amber controls, cyan status and cream text sit in graphite screen wells, with readable Verdana-like UI and mono character art. Buddy-list arrows and a quiet media strip supply the social reference. Small lock-ins and playback breathing stop with motion off. Keep proprietary platform marks, copied emoticons, glitter and joke typography out of the controls.

## Obsession Mode

Black, deep crimson and heavy condensed titles give the player the feel of a restrained psychological-thriller poster. Red belongs to selection, progress, playback and a few banners, leaving most surfaces dark. Thin fractures and cinematic album framing can suit industrial music, punk, dark synth and horror scores. Daily controls still need clean sans text; bright-red panels, gore and illegible horror lettering don't help.

## Crystal Audio

Contained glass surrounds the album art, with navy depth, cyan controls and quiet lavender glints. Pink is reserved for active playback rather than passive panels. Consistently rounded facets and lens-like circular controls distinguish it from the sharp poster and pixel themes.

Caustics and waterlight stay inside fixed layers so hover and animation don't move the layout. Keep blur and glow low enough for text and EQ to remain clear. Ambient, dream pop and electronic music fit the direction; museum-label serif type and sugary color everywhere belong elsewhere.

## Neon Burst

A blacklight print lab: black-violet ink, warm off-white text, ultraviolet edges, pear playback and oxidized teal responses. Registration marks, halftone fields and offset pressure edges provide the graphic rhythm. Brief shifts and pulses can make it energetic without constant glitching. Use plain readable body type, preserve static marks with motion off, and avoid the familiar cyan/magenta/lime rainbow stack.

## Monument

Albums sit like objects in a private museum, framed by limestone, gallery-wall tones, shadow blue and small copper/ivory accents. Collection labels use editorial type and compact mono details, with broad sightlines and quiet rails. Motion is almost still, allowing only a restrained lift where enabled. It suits sustained album listening; don't fill the negative space with props or turn it into a glossy hotel lobby.

## Analog Dossier

A listening case room with cabinet tabs, catalog cards, track ledgers and a seismograph signal. Off-white paper and oxidized stock sit against dark cabinets and black ink; burnt orange marks playback, selection and verification. Serif collection titles and mono source data make room for liner notes and format inspection. Keep paper movement mechanical and texture light enough to read. Fake detective props, copied poster collage and equal paper treatment on every surface flatten the idea.

## Cosmic Cinema

The album sits inside an event horizon, with orbital playback controls and sparse gravity/waveform rings. Abyss black, graphite and silver-white carry the observatory; cool blue is secondary and gold stays limited to favorites and tiny accents. Space Grotesk and IBM Plex Mono support the broad stage and quieter technical modules. Slow drift needs a static fallback. Keep it distant and restrained rather than a galaxy wallpaper or arcade.

## Frosted Void

Opaque black-acrylic panels hold illuminated artifacts and frosted circular controls. White/silver, smoke gray and a little calibration blue keep the ordinary shell severe; spectral color belongs to bubble film, active audio and EQ edges. Rounded panel glass contrasts with hard artifact frames. Pointer light, refraction and tuning hum must leave a static treatment when disabled. Avoid transparent low-contrast panels and recognizable poster imagery.

## Obsidian Glass

A softer black-glass player with floating rounded panels, large glossy artwork and mobile-like pills. White/silver controls and cyan playback/focus stay clear against smoked graphite; violet/pink refraction remains around edges and rings. Space Grotesk and mono technical labels keep it readable for daily listening. Calm lift and artwork breathing are optional. Don't let blur, rainbow color or indistinguishable black surfaces hide the controls.

## Dead Signal

An archived broadcast machine with black panels, bone type, cyan transmission and sparse crimson lock/warning state. Tape labels, towers, horizontal wave fields and a little contamination distinguish it from Obsession Mode's cleaner poster. Oswald headings and mono metadata stay readable. Subtle, Standard and Haunted detail levels vary the texture; no jumpscares, constant glitches or effects that pretend the app is broken. This entry preserves a design direction, not a promise to ship the retired artwork.

## Meme Machine

A music bot inside a dark group chat, with channel-like rows, reaction pills and licensed stickers. Blurple, online green and yellow carry the social cues. Mix Channels, Drop the Aux, Vibe Check and Bass Crimes are theme flavor; factual audio and destructive-action labels stay understandable. Low/Online/Terminally Online changes reaction density without hiding information. Keep motion optional and avoid copied platform marks, character memes or infinite bouncing.

## Poster Pop

A listening-party flyer with coral stock, cream paper, black ink, cyan stickers and yellow bursts. Large round playback controls, thick outlines and offset shadows let it be cheerful without making it hard to scan. Short lift/bounce responses become static sticker geometry with motion off. It suits party and workout playlists; avoid tiny controls, muddy color-on-color text and turning every surface into a different bright panel.

## Creator Layer

A second-monitor music window with dark channel rails, message-like track rows, compact voice-room controls and online-green playback. Room Style can adjust accent, mood, density, avatar shape, rows and activity detail, including the mini-player. Keep the core media controls literal and the dark surfaces distinct. Community-app ergonomics are a reference, not permission to copy logos, icons or a proprietary interface.

## Modular Signal

Lavender and blush fields carry square black circuitry, curved signal ribbons and a spoked vinyl instrument. Ink owns structure and shadow; lilac marks playing/selected state without becoming a large fill. Directional arrows and tabular indexes belong to headings and rows. Mechanical lift and slow spoke movement can support the layout, with static equivalents. Keep those few motifs coherent rather than reproducing a reference poster.

## Cut Sheet

A mastering document with aubergine depth, parchment surfaces, terracotta actions and ink registration ticks. Concentric lathe grooves and a resting tonearm frame artwork; only the playing row gets a brick-red CUT stamp. Condensed titles, tracked mono specifications and numbered manifests suit compact critical listening. Keep terracotta and sand out of large fills and don't substitute Modular Signal's spoke ring or heavy offset blocks.

## Acid Transit

Nightlife wayfinding built from fluorescent tape, offset depth and narrow pearlescent interference. Lime means confirmed playback/output; magenta means selection and focus. Pale lavender type stays readable on violet-black structure. Square bands with one clipped corner use a linear list deliberately, leaving room around the hero. Short directional responses work; fake hacking labels, tactical equipment and all-over glow don't.

## Ghost Index

A quiet systems archive with bone annotations on black, rare green confirmed state and coral intent. Editorial identity, mono evidence labels and a perspective track corridor give compact records room. The spectral-field mechanic must keep keyboard, click, context-menu, narrow and motion-off access intact. Centered playback comes from confirmed state. Keep source-tree/character/wireframe motifs restrained; no code rain, fake commands or texture over art.

## Violet//Violent

Transparent media slabs expose shell, circuit plane, artwork well, signal bus and cast shadow. Violet marks selection; cyan lights only for confirmed playback/output. Pearl content and peach reflection keep the optical hardware readable against black.

Memory Cascade stacks those complete objects around one confirmed position, with keyboard, pointer and context-menu support. Motion-off/conserve keep the layered depth and borders. It suits tactile physical-media references without copied devices, controller symbols, fake lettering or a universal vaporwave gradient.

## Abyssal Press

Oversized type forms layers around a confirmed depth line, with gel apertures and narrow utility rails. Magenta marks intent, cyan confirmed playback and amber warnings. Pressure Stack compresses neighboring track labels above/below the current plate; a request doesn't move the datum until the host confirms it. Keep the broad print field readable and static when motion is off. Avoid literal aquarium props, copied lettering and invented coordinates.

## Axis Break (C3 experiment)

An open mineral-paper field is cut by one continuous oblique signal seam. Oxide marks selection, graphite marks CURRENT / PAUSED, and vermilion/amber appears only with main is-playing or mini playing state. The linear list supplies browsing without another invented mechanic. This recorded C3 candidate had not passed propagation, compliance or acceptance review; registration wasn't approval.

## Tideplot (C3 controlled-regression candidate)

Tracks braid through a pale plotting field around a movable clearing. Violet belongs to browse intent; confirmed playback owns the cyan/dark aperture. Current Weave lets focus move the clearing, while a second click or Enter/Space requests playback and only host activeId moves the playback aperture. Narrow layouts rebraid vertically. The recorded controlled-regression candidate still needed independent relationship, functional and caliber review.

## Aftergarden (C3 process field-test candidate)

Browsed tracks remain cuttings on the light side of a graftline. Only host-confirmed playback crosses into the matte afterfield and opens the signal bloom; focus remains labeled NOT PLAYING. Pending/failure belongs to the requested cutting, while pause keeps a dormant anchor. The mini is its own condensed confirmed cutting, not a shrunken main browser. This C3 field-test slice hadn't established sustained usability, accessibility, recovery, midpoint acceptance or broad propagation.

## Vesperfold (C3 shared-strata vertical slice)

Browsing cuts one irregular acoustic mass into ordered strata. A selected notch and bounded color trace stay separate from the amber confirmed-playback suture. Shared Strata supports pointer focus, second-click/keyboard activation requests and ordered traversal; only the host update moves confirmation. Narrow layouts rotate/resequence the relationship. Its read-only information profile doesn't own playback. Bounded painted tests existed, but C3 remained REPAIR: long-library use, full manual interaction, accessibility, recovery and acceptance were still open.
